runtimeEmailRole.justification: Built-in role used because deployment users cannot safely receive roleDefinitions/write. This is broader than the former custom role: at the selected Communication resource it permits resource and email-service management, deletion, and key retrieval/regeneration. Keep the assignment resource-scoped and review changes to the built-in role.

runtimeWebPubSubRole.justification: Built-in role used because deployment users cannot safely receive roleDefinitions/write. It grants all Web PubSub data actions (including closing connections and managing group/user permissions) instead of the former four-action custom role. It has no management actions, so it cannot read keys or re-enable local auth. Group grants remain server-selected from signed token scopes.

runtimeFoundryDataRole.justification: Built-in preview role used because deployment users cannot safely receive roleDefinitions/write. It grants all Cognitive Services data actions at the Foundry project scope, broader than the former AIServices/* custom role, but no management actions, so no key retrieval or account changes. Agent business access remains bounded by OAuth-delegated MCP/API tokens and tool policies.

azdDeployerAccessManagement.servicePrincipalJustification: Fallback for tighter subscriptions where the user cannot deploy: the GitHub Actions service principal holds Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator at subscription scope. That grant must carry the reviewed condition: only allowlisted role IDs, and only ServicePrincipal assignees, for both role-assignment write and delete. Users hold no Azure deployment permissions in this path.
